title: Review: read-only Sol review of the A5 capability integration PR (full diff)
description:
READ-ONLY REVIEW. Do not edit, create, or delete any file; do not commit; do not push. Your only writes are bd notes on this bead and closing it.

SCOPE: the full diff of branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 against origin/main (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`, 73 files) — one PR carrying eight beads: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4 (character suffocation recovery gate, migration 0032, set_suffocation, calc breath formulas), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5 (player-character death rules for encounter combatants, migration 0033), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.6 (adjust_hp knockOut), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.3 (adjust_exhaustion, derived level-4 HP maximum, level-6 death), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.11.4 (expend_ammunition / recover_ammunition, migration 0034), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.10.3 (roll_retained_check / resolve_retained_check / end_retained_check, set_surprised derived from comparisons, migration 0035), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.6 (hydra Multiple Heads curated mechanic, tracked head count, derived reaction allowance, migration 0036), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.5 (action:use-an-object ordinaryInteractionRuleRef -> rule:other-activity-on-your-turn, importer). Run `bd show` on each bead and on eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 for the specs and acceptance criteria.

AUTHORITY: AGENTS.md; docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md (profile rules-clause-complete); ADR 0020 §§2-3 (dice, arithmetic, atomic state mutation, resource accounting, state integrity are deterministic; adjudicated outcomes still pass through those boundaries); docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendments A3-A5 and invariants 12-13; ADR 0015 (migration-first schema); docs/importer-fix-protocol.md for the importer parts; the committed SRD source text for every rule (packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, records use the `key` field).

METHOD (review the mechanism, not the narrative):
1. For each capability, print the governing SRD source text beside the implementation and check source fidelity of every engine rule (thresholds, tie semantics, rounding, ordering, what counts as damage/healing, lifecycle start/end).
2. Check every model-facing surface (tool descriptions, schemas, Hybrid Contract in protocol.ts, known-limit statements in ruleKnownLimits.ts, error/rejection messages) against the real code: truthful, no model-side arithmetic/comparison or model-held canonical state offered as a fallback, target domain correct (character vs combatant), no stale wording from the pre-capability disclosures.
3. State integrity: atomicity (single transaction), invariants across the full state space (alive/dying/stable/dead, monster vs player-character rules, recovery block, exhaustion levels, closed vs active combat instances, missing/malformed rows), concentration and attunement side effects, campaign-actor sync, provenance conventions, deterministic ids/replay, write paths that bypass established helpers (mutateState, claimItem, removeItem), migration correctness (constraints, indexes, data preservation, contiguity, schema snapshot).
4. Write paths that let a model persist an unsupported/derived value (the A5 forbidden-substitution class), and any place a refusal could be bypassed through another tool (e.g. add_condition, update_combatant status, rest, level-up).
5. Test evidence: does each acceptance criterion have a test that distinguishes the bad state from the good state? Name missing evidence only where a real requirement is unprotected.
6. Sibling search: for each defect, look for the same class elsewhere in the diff.

REPORT with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes`, then `bd close <this bead>`. One entry per finding: ID (S1, S2, ...), severity (blocker / should-fix / nit), file:line, the violated requirement and its authority, a concrete failure scenario (inputs -> wrong state), and the minimal fix. Then a short list of what you checked and found correct. Apply the review policy's "From observation to finding" test: an observation without an operative requirement is "no requirement" in one line, not a finding. Do not stop at the first defect; batch everything you can find.
acceptance_criteria: Findings recorded in bd notes; no file changes; bead closed by the reviewer.
notes:
S1 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1776
Requirement/authority: Opted-in combatants must follow the PC death rules (eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5); SRD rule:death-saving-throws says damage at 0 HP equal to or greater than the HP maximum causes instant death. ADR 0020 §§2–3 owns the transition deterministically.
Failure: Start a 20/20 PC-rules combatant, apply hpDelta:-20, then hpDelta:-20. Registry probe leaves status:dying, failures:1, rather than dead. The same branch affects stable combatants, critical damage, and exhaustion-reduced maxima. Character applyDamage already checks the threshold.
Minimal fix: Check damage-at-zero against effectiveHpMax before adding failures, sharing the character transition where practical; preserve atomic actor/concentration updates.
Permanent evidence: Generalized boundary regression over dying/stable, critical/noncritical, and effective maxima, with damage below/equal/above the maximum. This protects a lethal rule boundary rather than one example. Owner: .19.5.7.5; material repair.
S2 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1452
Requirement/authority: SRD rule:death-saving-throws resets both counters only on regaining HP or becoming stable; suffocation does neither. .19.5.7.5 requires PC-rule parity and .19.5.7.4 owns the recovery gate.
Failure: PC-rules combatant drops to 0, takes a critical hit (two failures), then set_suffocation(event:drop). Registry probe resets failures from 2 to 0. Clearing and re-entering suffocation can repeatedly erase death-save progress. The character beginSuffocation correctly preserves existing dying counters.
Minimal fix: Preserve both counters when the target was already dying; reset only on a genuine initial drop from another life state. Clear obsolete stable schedules when leaving stable.
Permanent evidence: Generalized character/combatant parity for suffocation entry from alive, dying with nonzero successes/failures, and stable, plus drop/breathe/drop sequences. The durable invariant is no unearned counter reset. Owner: .19.5.7.5/.19.5.7.4; material repair.
S3 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1761
Requirement/authority: .19.5.7.5 makes PC lifecycle transitions engine-owned; .19.5.7.3 requires level-six death; .19.3.4.6 requires death when all heads die. SRD rule:healing requires revival before a dead creature regains HP; ADR 0020 state integrity forbids substituting an explicit status for these outcomes.
Failure: A PC-rules 20/20 combatant receives adjust_exhaustion(delta:6), becoming dead at 10 HP. update_combatant(status:alive) revives it while exhaustion remains 6. Explicit escaped/inactive statuses also bypass the damage-derived lifecycle branch. Sibling: after five separate fire-damage head losses, a hydra is dead with heads:0 and HP:47; hpDelta:1 changes it to alive with heads:0 because the no-head death guard only checks the transition to zero. Both resurrection scenarios reproduced through the registry.
Minimal fix: Derive mandatory HP/death transitions before accepting status changes; preserve terminal death absent an explicit revival operation, and enforce zero-head death as a state invariant on every write. Preserve the authorized knockout exception.
Permanent evidence: Generalized transition matrix varying current death state, exhaustion, head count, hpDelta and explicit statuses. It must distinguish legitimate knockout/status changes from lifecycle bypasses. Owner: .19.5.7.5/.19.5.7.3/.19.3.4.6; material repair.
S4 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1180
Requirement/authority: ADR 0020 §3 persistent state/identity integrity; existing campaign_actor is the durable recurring-actor owner (ADR 0012 and this module's actor/projection contract). .19.5.7.5 says opt-in is for good; .19.5.7.4 and .19.3.4.6 require persisted recovery/head state.
Failure: Opt actor A into PC rules, suffocate it, close encounter C1, and start C2 with the same actor. Probe creates A at 0 HP/status:dying but death_rules:monster, counters:0 and recovery_block:null; healing succeeds without breathing and leaves dying at positive HP. Likewise, a recurring hydra's heads reset to source initialHeads rather than its tracked current count. Actor sync currently copies HP/conditions/status only.
Minimal fix: Make durable actor state own the selected death rules, counters, recovery block/schedule and head lifecycle, then transfer/project that state atomically across encounters. Do not infer these facts from status or reset them from the base record.
Permanent evidence: Generalized close/reopen continuity tests for dying/suffocating/stable actors and hydras with lost/regrown heads, including subsequent healing/death saves. This protects canonical actor identity across projections. Owner: integration/.19.5.7.5/.19.3.4.6; material repair.
S5 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1514
Requirement/authority: ADR 0020 state integrity and existing actor/projection ownership require an obsolete encounter row not to overwrite newer canonical actor state; SRD rule:healing prohibits automatic revival of a dead creature.
Failure: Stabilize actor A in C1 and obtain its recovery deadline, close C1, project A into C2 and kill it there. advance_time to the old deadline heals the archived C1 row and syncCombatantActor overwrites A to alive/1 HP while C2 remains dead/0 HP. Reproduced. The new death-save, stabilization and suffocation helpers also read arbitrary archived ids without checking which projection still owns the actor.
Minimal fix: Resolve recovery and other lifecycle writes against the authoritative actor/current projection, invalidate or transfer superseded schedules, and refuse stale historical writes that can sync into a newer actor revision. Continue supporting legitimate recovery after combat ends.
Permanent evidence: Generalized superseded-projection tests: heal, damage, death and new encounter between schedule creation and expiry; exercise the sibling lifecycle tools against old ids. This protects against stale asynchronous writes. Owner: .19.5.7.5/integration; material repair.
S6 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/ammunition.ts:78
Requirement/authority: .19.5.11.4 selects deterministic recovery accounting and atomic custody/destruction; SRD rule:weapon-properties permits recovery of half the expended ammunition after the battle. ADR 0020 §3 resource accounting and A5 forbidden-substitution rules prohibit bypassing that step through another tool.
Failure: Give four arrows, expend_ammunition(quantity:4), claim_item on the returned expendedInventoryId, close combat, then recover_ammunition. Registry probe retains all four in custody and reports recovered:0/destroyed:0/movedAway:4. Expended rows are ordinary dropped rows; context explicitly presents nearby rows as claimable. The existing test at ammunition.test.ts:265 covers one early claim but authorizes rather than closes this bypass. Re-claim/re-expend can also make multiple expenditure records alias one physical row.
Minimal fix: Mark tracked expenditure as reserved for deterministic recovery and enforce that ownership across claim/transfer/reacquire paths; perform the allowed custody change only through the accounting operation, with an explicit separate adjudicated exception if needed.
Permanent evidence: Generalized custody/accounting invariant across ordinary inventory tools and repeated expenditure, proving total returned cannot exceed the engine-derived entitlement and physical rows cannot be counted twice. Owner: .19.5.11.4; material repair.
S7 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/rest.ts:659
Requirement/authority: SRD rule:long-rest restores all lost HP at completion; condition:exhaustion reduces exhaustion by one with food/drink, with its effects ending below the relevant level. .19.5.7.3 explicitly requires long-rest interoperability.
Failure: Base max:20, exhaustion:4, current HP:3; complete a qualifying long rest with food/drink. Probe ends at exhaustion:3, effective maximum:20, current HP:10. Healing occurs against the old half maximum, then exhaustion is reduced, leaving half the lost HP unrestored.
Minimal fix: Apply the authorized exhaustion reduction before computing/applying the final long-rest HP restoration, all in the existing transaction; compute/report benefits from the resulting effective maximum.
Permanent evidence: Generalized long-rest transition test for exhaustion 3/4/5 and food/drink present/absent, proving current HP equals the final effective maximum. Existing level-two rest coverage cannot distinguish this failure. Owner: .19.5.7.3; material repair.
S8 | blocker | packages/core/src/character/levelUpEngine.ts:1362
Requirement/authority: SRD rule:healing forbids HP above the maximum; condition:exhaustion halves that maximum at level four. ADR 0020 state integrity applies to every canonical write; this PR introduces the derived maximum and touches the level-up bypass gate.
Failure: Base max:20, exhaustion:4, current HP:10. Apply an ordinary fighter level-up raising sheet max by six. Probe persists base max:26/current HP:16, although effective maximum is 13. projectToLiveCharacter writes the full sheet increment directly through mutateState instead of respecting the derived maximum. Sibling admission paths are existing level-four rows on upgrade and actor projection from a supplied/raw HP maximum.
Minimal fix: Preserve sheet hp_max, but apply/validate current-HP changes against effectiveHpMax through the canonical HP boundary; audit initialization/projection/upgrade paths for the same invariant.
Permanent evidence: Generalized current-HP/effective-maximum invariant over progression at exhaustion levels below/above four and HP gains with odd/even maxima, with representative admission coverage. Owner: .19.5.7.3/integration; material repair.
S9 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/party.ts:76
Requirement/authority: condition:exhaustion's level-four maximum is operative game state; ADR 0020 state integrity and the review bead require truthful model-facing state. listParty is the shared party-prompt/CLI roster projection, while this PR changes the detailed character snapshot to report effectiveHpMax.
Failure: A base-max-20 character with exhaustion four and current HP ten is reported as HP 10/20 in PartyMember/CLI roster and the multi-member prompt, while the detailed character snapshot reports HP 10/10. For a nonacting member, the roster is the available compact HP projection, so the DM receives an incorrect mechanical maximum.
Minimal fix: Derive PartyMember.hpMax from its validated conditions via effectiveHpMax, consistently with character/combatant/actor displays.
Permanent evidence: Generalized projection parity test for exhausted and nonexhausted party members, including a nonacting member; one shared-data assertion covers both prompt and CLI consumers without duplicating rendering tests. Owner: .19.5.7.3; non-material localized repair.
S10 | blocker | packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRollRetainedCheck.ts:75; packages/core/src/orchestrator/contextAssembler.ts:605
Requirement/authority: .19.5.10.3 requires comparison of an engine-recorded retained identity without rerolling; SRD rule:hiding keeps that total until discovered/stopped. ADR 0020 §§2–3 keeps canonical state in the engine, not model memory.
Failure: roll_retained_check persists a random opaque id and only returns it in that call. Start/resume a subsequent model context after the call history leaves the bounded context: active checks/ids appear in neither StateSnapshot nor assembled context, and no registered read tool enumerates them (memory_drilldown reads summaries/scene prose, not retained-check rows or tool traces). Probe confirms the active id is absent from freshly assembled context. resolve/end tools require the missing id, so the model must remember canonical identity outside the persisted read boundary or reroll.
Minimal fix: Expose campaign-scoped active retained-check identity, participant and label through bounded context or a deterministic read tool, respecting visibility, and use that path after resume. Keep the retained total engine-owned.
Permanent evidence: Generalized resume/read-consumer regression: create a check, discard the model/tool conversation, assemble/read fresh context, resolve the original id without consuming another hider roll; omit ended checks. Owner: .19.5.10.3; material consumer integration.
S11 | blocker | packages/core/data/migrations/0036_combatant_heads.sql:1; packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts:396
Requirement/authority: .19.3.4.6 requires tracked head state and engine-derived reaction allowance for the curated Multiple Heads mechanic. ADR 0015 owns upgrade correctness; ADR 0020 requires canonical lifecycle inputs instead of silently substituting a default for unknown state.
Failure: Create a full-HP active hydra in a database at migration 0035, then apply 0036. A real migration probe leaves head_count:null; begin_turn grants one reaction, and update_combatant(hpDelta:-25) lowers HP to 147 without losing a head. New-encounter initialization works, but upgraded active encounters have no initialization, unsupported-state marker or refusal. Existing damaged hydras also cannot safely have their current heads reconstructed from base HP.
Minimal fix: Give existing applicable rows an explicit upgrade/admission disposition. Initialize only facts that can be established from valid stored/source state; require an explicit repair for unknown historical head state and refuse affected operations until repaired. Do not silently treat missing head state as supported one-head behavior.
Permanent evidence: Migration integration regression with an existing active hydra, comparing supported fresh state with upgraded known/unknown state; assert either correct tracked behavior or an explicit bounded refusal, never silent fallback. Owner: .19.3.4.6/integration; material repair.
S12 | should-fix | packages/core/src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts:54; packages/core/src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts:173; packages/core/src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts:204
Requirement/authority: Design amendments A3/A4, invariant 12 and each capability bead's R0 require a known limit to describe an actual trap; positive rule-to-tool mappings belong in the tool contract and were expressly retired. The governing SRD rule:suffocating also grants CON-based survival rounds after breath runs out.
Failure: After the capabilities land, the food/water/speed and surprise entries still present positive operation recipes as partial known limits without identifying a remaining trap. The suffocation recipe additionally says a character whose breath runs out should drop at the start of its turn, without requiring expiry of suffocation_survival_rounds first; following that instruction drops a CON +2 character before its two survival rounds expire.
Minimal fix: Re-derive these entries under R0: retire entries with no specific residual trap, retain only the actual bounded limitations, and put accurate target/timing instructions in tool descriptions. Explicitly distinguish breath exhaustion from expiry of the survival interval.
Permanent evidence: Keep the existing R0/statement-separation evidence and add a source-backed timing/contract assertion where that instruction survives. Avoid treating the existence of a tool mapping as proof that a known limit is required. Owner: integration/.19.5.7.3/.19.5.10.3/.19.5.7.4; non-material disclosure repair.
S13 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts:940; packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:470
Requirement/authority: .19.3.4.6 selects the full tracked head lifecycle; SRD creature:hydra regrows heads at the end of its turn unless fire intervenes, without requiring an available action. rule:suffocating blocks HP recovery, not passage of the turn boundary or head-state settlement. ADR 0020 owns these transitions atomically.
Failure: Opt a hydra into PC rules and deal 172 damage in one turn: it is dying at 0 HP with four heads and one head owed for regrowth. begin_turn on that unavailable participant immediately completes its turn without settling heads; the next participant starts with no regrowth and the hydra remains four-headed/dying rather than regrowing two heads and recovering 20 HP. Sibling: lose a head, begin the hydra's available turn, then suffocate it. Beginning the next participant calls regrowth healing, which throws 'cannot regain hit points while suffocating'; the transaction rolls back and the turn cannot advance.
Minimal fix: Settle passive head effects on every own-turn end, including skipped/unavailable turns. When HP recovery is blocked, commit eligible head regrowth and the turn boundary while suppressing the HP gain; continue excluding dead creatures and fire-suppressed regrowth.
Permanent evidence: Generalized turn-end lifecycle coverage for alive/unconscious/dying/dead, with recovery block and fire varied. Assert head state, actual HP gained and successful boundary advancement together. Owner: .19.3.4.6/.19.5.7.5 integration; material repair.
S14 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/exhaustion.ts:26
Requirement/authority: The selected condition:exhaustion source says the level-four HP maximum is halved, without a minimum-one exception; .19.5.7.3 and ADR 0020 require source-grounded deterministic math. Implementation commentary and a test are not authority for adding that exception (AGENTS Permanent Test Evidence).
Failure: effectiveHpMax(1, [{id:'exhaustion',level:4}]) returns 1, while all larger odd maxima use floor(max/2). The implementation deliberately overrides its halving calculation at this boundary to avoid an HP clamp consequence, and exhaustion.test.ts:302 makes that invented exception permanent.
Minimal fix: Establish and apply one source-backed halving/rounding rule uniformly, then handle any resulting zero-maximum lifecycle explicitly; do not avoid that analysis by inventing a minimum. If a minimum-one exception is intended as a product rule, it needs accepted authority before implementation/test endorsement.
Permanent evidence: A proportionate generalized boundary test for one, odd and even maxima across character/combatant projections, with the resulting zero-HP lifecycle asserted under the established rule. Preserve source-fidelity intent rather than updating expected output to match the present exception. Owner: .19.5.7.3; localized behavioral repair.
S15 | should-fix | packages/core/test/ruleDispositions.test.ts:273
Requirement/authority: Design A5 and invariant 13 explicitly retain the gap registry, report projection and its permanent regression evidence even after the current registry becomes empty. AGENTS permits staged retained responsibility and requires evidence that distinguishes the protected behavior.
Failure: The projection test now asserts expected=[] and compares the report and unresolved-work projection to that empty collection. Removing the producer's entire nonempty-gap projection would still pass, so the retained machinery has lost the evidence for its staged responsibility when the next gap is registered.
Minimal fix: Keep the real-pack empty-registry assertion, and exercise one registered fixture gap through the actual report producer, asserting its operation, owner and unresolved-work entry. Use a narrow fixture/injection boundary rather than additional expensive audit machinery.
Permanent evidence: This generalized nonempty projection test is the missing invariant itself; it must fail when projection is removed or ownership metadata is dropped. Owner: integration/A5; non-material evidence repair.
Review disposition: CHANGES REQUESTED. Reviewed the full 73-file integration diff at HEAD 1165938ccded1a78b6fb8c8e7af15e0a3aac64b4 against origin/main 18c1b30575d082afcc6c2df76e981bcb7be7a9d1; review and integration branches were identical. S1–S15 are the complete finding batch. Material lifecycle, persistence, upgrade and accounting fixes require re-review of the affected implementation and sibling paths under the rules-clause-complete profile.

Checked and found correct:
- Character suffocation gates healing, stabilization and death-save recovery while preserving existing dying counters; breathing/death clears the block. Normal concentration/attunement death effects and stable recovery scheduling remain integrated.
- Knockout consumes temporary HP first, overrides ordinary melee lethal overflow only when selected, and enters stable/unconscious with the existing recovery schedule. Normal exhaustion increments/caps and level-six consequence work on both target types; ordinary HP paths use the derived maximum.
- Uncomplicated ammunition expenditure/recovery paths preserve item identity, derive even/odd per-group quantities, enforce location/battle eligibility, use canonical custody/destruction helpers atomically, and reject repeated settlement. Expenditure IDs are deterministic; S6 addresses the separate custody bypass.
- Retained-check comparison reuses the stored hider roll, rolls only a fresh opposing check where requested, applies passive adjustments and correct comparison/tie behavior, and validates campaign/identity/activity. Surprise derives from validated comparison records; supplied surprised lists and reaction totals are rejected. Pre-encounter checks are supported.
- Normal living-hydra paths aggregate the 25-damage threshold per turn, lose at most one head per turn, suppress regrowth after fire, derive extra reactions from tracked heads, and apply ordinary regrowth/healing. Curated Multiple Heads fields match the committed source.
- Use-an-object now references rule:other-activity-on-your-turn. Generated pack regeneration is exact, including records/manifest, source inventory and coverage, source-region ledger, field provenance and relationships. Migrations 0032–0036 are contiguous and schema-snapshot/parity tests pass; S11 concerns semantic upgrade state rather than SQL shape.

Read-only validation: npm run typecheck passed (forced build); npm run test passed with 5650 passed/3 documented skipped tests across 320 passed/2 skipped files; focused capability tests passed (214 tests); npm run check passed without fixes; npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack passed with 1799 records and zero added/removed/changed records. Throwaway probes reproduced the failure scenarios. No tracked file was changed, no Git/PR write was made, and no other bead was modified.
